extracted.intended_audience: mathematics instructors and prospective authors submitting to MAA Convergence (secondary and collegiate levels)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for preparing and submitting articles to MAA Convergence, an online refereed journal about the history of mathematics and its use in teaching, aimed at secondary and collegiate mathematics instructors. Covers scope, required focus, accepted article types, and permissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dual requirement: historical context and classroom use
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions to MAA Convergence must both place mathematical concepts or solutions in historical context and indicate how the history of the concepts might be used to teach mathematics to today’s students.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although the realm of possible classroom connections is infinite, the list in the “Connecting History to the Classroom” link offers several common ways articles bring together history and teaching, along with examples of how these connections were realized in existing publications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aims and scope — journal focus
rubrics_metrics.description: MAA Convergence is a refereed online journal about the history of mathematics and its use in teaching.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aimed at mathematics instructors at both the secondary and collegiate levels; includes topics from grades 8–16 mathematics (with special emphasis on topics from grades 8–14).

rubrics_metrics.name: Topical coverage (subjects and grade levels)
rubrics_metrics.description: Articles should address mathematics topics appropriate to grades 8–16, especially grades 8–14, including algebra, combinatorics, synthetic and analytic geometry, trigonometry, probability and statistics, elementary functions, calculus, differential equations, and linear algebra.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary article type — Classroom Resources
rubrics_metrics.description: The journal’s main article types are Classroom Resources: pieces that place historical material in a form useful for teaching.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classroom Resources may include (but are not limited to) guided readings of primary sources; self-contained classroom lessons; exercises from historical treatises or textbooks; pedagogical explorations inspired by historical material; alternative approaches to mathematical concepts; course outlines; classroom discussion prompts; suggestions for student research projects; uses of primary sources in the classroom; and discussions of practices and philosophies involved in incorporating history into pedagogy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classroom Capsules (short classroom enhancements)
rubrics_metrics.description: Classroom Capsules are short articles similar to Classroom Resources that offer briefer and more focused classroom enhancements or teaching moments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended to be concise and narrowly focused on a single classroom enhancement or teaching idea drawn from history.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematical Treasures (pictorial work)
rubrics_metrics.description: Mathematical Treasures are pictorial articles featuring images of rare, significant, or unusual books in the history of mathematics as well as other artifacts, with descriptive and explanatory text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In your submission, please select Pictorial Work as the article type and Mathematical Treasures as the section heading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reports (classroom implementation descriptions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reports are descriptions and observations from authors’ implementations into a mathematics classroom of historical material drawn from one of the journal’s published articles or from the wider literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports should document implementation and observations, showing how historical material was used in practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expository Articles (factual history with classroom relevance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Expository Articles explain, describe, and provide factual information about the history of mathematics and its use in teaching mathematics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classroom connections in expository articles may not be as explicitly discussed as those in Classroom Resources, but relevance to teaching should be clear or suggested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Articles (original primary-source research)
rubrics_metrics.description: Research Articles present original primary-source research in support of the teaching of mathematics through the history of mathematics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These should provide novel historical scholarship that informs or supports pedagogical uses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article Series (thematically organized compilations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Article Series are compilations of separately published materials organized by a unifying theme in the history or pedagogy of mathematics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Series submissions should demonstrate a coherent unifying theme across the compiled materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Essays (short analytical pieces)
rubrics_metrics.description: Essays are short analyses, specifically those that address reasons for or approaches to using the history of mathematics to teach mathematics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Essays should be concise and focused on rationale or pedagogical approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interviews (scholar conversations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Interviews are transcribed or recorded conversations with scholars who have used the history of mathematics to teach mathematics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions should present useful insights into practice or pedagogy drawn from the interviewee’s experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Orations (speeches and presentations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Orations are reproductions of speeches or oral presentations on the use of the history of mathematics in the teaching of mathematics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These should be relevant to instructional practice or historical perspectives on teaching.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target readership — instructors as audience
rubrics_metrics.description: Articles should be written with mathematics instructors (secondary and collegiate levels) as the primary audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contributions are meant to help instructors enrich students’ learning by teaching mathematics using its history.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusivity encouragement
rubrics_metrics.description: The journal encourages submissions from all backgrounds, regardless of career stage, geography, or other defining characteristics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MAA Convergence aims to be a truly inclusive journal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reprint permission policy for institutional members
rubrics_metrics.description: General permission is granted to institutional members of the MAA for noncommercial reproduction in limited quantities of individual articles (in whole or in part) provided a complete reference is made to the source.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reprint permission for other uses should be requested from Taylor and Francis using the provided form.
